title: Non-bypassable human sign-off: why SEWA enforces radiologist review at the database layer
subtitle: UI-level review can be skipped. Database-layer sign-off cannot.
excerpt: Most clinical AI platforms place human review at the user interface level — a prompt the radiologist can dismiss, a modal they can close, a workflow they can override. content:
The problem with UI-level review

Most clinical AI platforms place human review at the user interface level — a prompt the radiologist can dismiss, a modal they can close, a workflow they can override. In high-pressure clinical environments, these UI-level safeguards are frequently bypassed. A radiologist reading 200 studies in a shift does not want to stop and approve every AI notification. The result is a system that is designed to require human oversight but is engineered to allow it to be skipped.

SEWA takes a different approach. Sign-off is enforced at the database layer: a finding is never persisted as an approved clinical result unless a consultant radiologist has explicitly accepted it. There is no UI prompt the user can dismiss, no administrator override, and no bypass path. Human oversight is structural — enforced by the data model itself, not by a workflow setting.
author: Dolapo Ariyo
